study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: perceived social support during the postnatal period
birth before arriving at the hospital
perceived control during labour and birth
cohort: 1824 women who gave birth in one large hospital in England
finding: Several factors were associated with birth-related post-traumatic stress symptoms, including being Black, higher pre-pregnancy BMI, history of mental illness, birth before hospital arrival, emergency caesarean section, severe maternal morbidity, neonatal complications, lower perceived control during labour, and lower perceived social support.
mod_finding: Women who underwent an emergency caesarean section showed more symptoms of post-traumatic stress.
